*sighs* I have been the number one advocate for this series ever since I read the first book and even more so when I read the second. But I am a little disappointed with the ending in this one.

I thought back in Earth & Sky that Win was SO BORING like zero personality and was not a good love interest for Skylar who had so much to offer. And when he said he was just kissing her as an experiment, I was glad because Skylar could move on and find someone who would actually care about her and her interests. Enter Jule in A Clouded Sky. He was everything Win wasn't and there was so much less Win in this one that I thought we were finally done with him being cast as more than a friend for Skylar. But you know YA, can't have a series without a love triangle. So in A Sky Unbroken, of course I am going to be disappointed that Jule was never endgame. Because I don't understand why build it up so much just to tear it all down.

I was okay with Skylar not forgiving Jule right away, even okay with her maybe not forgiving him in this book at all -- as long as it was hinted that she could do that and could move forward with him. But nope. That hope was dashed around 36% of the book and I was not okay with it.

I also thought that Win was almost out of character in this one because he never showed that he was capable of thinking and planning the operations -- only that he was able to go off script to get what he wanted. I wasn't a fan of him being in charge. I don't know, I just don't like Win. I didn't think he was developed enough in the last two novels to have his own pov AND take charge at the same time. I think it was asking too much of me as a reader to be okay with this.

Skylar was still great. I think she had a very central role but I'm not sure I'm okay with how she treated the other Earthlings throughout the novel. She wanted to show that Earth was strong and did the opposite. And I'm glad she owned up to it but I don't think she would have done that to begin with.

I was only okay with the conclusion of the overall arc and story. I thought the penultimate conclusion of what happened was kind of obvious from the beginning and I'm not sure I liked the path to get there. I think the twist (if you could call it that) was a little out there since here was nothing really leading to it that suggested it in the last two novels. It seemed like it relied heavily on the readers believing that these people would hide this fact from their own kind and that it could happen. I wasn't a fan.

It was good but not great. I wasn't too impressed with how some things turned out because it didn't seem like the rest of the novels were leading to what took place. It was more like this one did a 180 degree turn to face something else and I was a little disappointed.

Jamie, AKA Saint, is a retired Navy SEAL who works for his former commander handling dangerous, non-military assignments world-wide.  On his return from his most recent assignment, Sugar Darling picks him up at the airport, and annoyed does not begin to describe his feelings about that.  Saint knows Sugar, and her ditsy, carefree attitude rubs him the wrong way  or perhaps not?  Something about Sugar makes him want her in a way he hasn't wanted anyone for years, ever since he made some serious life decisions and became Saint.

Sugar has made some serious life changes in the last few years as well, but the necessity of hers have a critical impact on her present and ongoing life in a way that Jamies does not.  She escaped from an abusive husband and is trying to start a new life, but she is also ever fearful that her husband, and her father, will catch up to her.  Sugar wasn't always who she is nowinstead, she was once Hannah, an abuse victim who was afraid of everything.  Unable to cope with removing herself from the situation, Sugar took over, and Sugar decides what she does in life by doing the opposite of what Hannah would do.

As you might expect, Sugars past catches up with her and Saint and his friends have to jump into action to help her, although being back in her husbands home with her dad unexpectedly there too just might be too much of a threat to overcome.

First let me say that I love this entire series and am looking forward to book 4.  This can definitely be read as a stand-alone, and if you haven't read the previous books, you will likely want to.  I have mixed feelings about this book  no question that I enjoyed it.  I was happy to see Saint get his story and it was fun to see it unfold.  My mixed feelings come in when Saint falls for Sugar, and Sugar isn't actually the real person, but rather she is the adopted personality put in place to cope with and escape a life of abuse.  The narrative seems to indicate that this is an intentional adoption of personality rather than a personality disorder/true split personality.  However, it seems odd when I think about it to have a HEA between two characters, one of whom got to know the others adopted personality, not the real one.  This is the only reason I gave four stars rather than five.  Perhaps I am over-thinking this and just need to sit back and enjoy the big picture of the story.

I remind myself that shes not mine.  That still doesnt stop the caveman in my head from growling.  Mine.

A surprise connection throws them together yet again.  Wesleys got his work cut out for him convincing Mac to give them a chance.  And Mac just cant accept that this man is really interested in her, the REAL her.

Goodbye to the Dead is the seventh (and last, to date) of the Jonathan Stride novels.  It is also something of a prequel.  The story begins with Strides second wife, Cindy, still very much alive.  She has dropped off a doctor friend, Janine Snow, at her home.  The doctor has an argument with her husband and goes off to take a shower.  When she finishes her shower she finds her husband dead, shot through the forehead, and some of her expensive jewelry missing.  The gun is missing as well, but the doctor is arrested and tried for second-degree murder.  Stride thinks her guilty; his wife thinks that she is innocent.

This story (including the trial) occupies approximately 60% of the story.  From there we flash forward to present time.  Stride has had his affair with Maggie and is now reunited with Serena.  They are working a human trafficking case in Duluth.  One woman has been murdered; another is missing.  In the course of this investigation evidence is recovered that is linked to the Janine Snow murder/investigation/trial.  The evidence may prove to be exculpatory, but since this is a Brian Freeman novel we must remain open to the possibility of a twist or two.

The novel is rock solid.  The plot, subplot and personal story plot are all integrated nicely and the time levels are mixed very smoothly.  Even though there are some unattractive characteristics of one of the primary characters (Dr. Snow) we come to care about her and certainly want to learn of her guilt or innocence. Sy's story started with a gut wrenching and heartbreaking discovery. His quiet and moody and quite sullen behavior makes sense and the pieces start falling into place. Told with some of Sy's flashbacks, we see him before he became part of the Knights Rebels. When Holly, Kadence's best friend, meets him she doesn't know he's part of the MC only that he's big, tatted and beautiful. She wants more so she makes her move. What surprises her is that Sy doesn't react. At all.

During this time the club is having trouble with Kadence's ex-fiancee so Sy has to keep his eye on her her and Holly. What becomes obvious to Holly is that Sy is holding back but she doesn't know why. Eventually Sy's attraction to Holly pushes him and Holly together twice before he leaves her high and dry. When Kadence's ex attacks and hurts her and Holly, Holly isn't the same outgoing and silly girl anymore and Sy is worried he's lost her before he can even have her.

This series has grabbed me by the heart and hasn't let go since I started. Sy and Holly's story is no different. These two tortured souls have found each other and as hard as their circumstances are to overcome, together they start making their way. I loved watching Sy begin a friendship with Holly. I had the honor of working with Mary E Palmerin on this book.  While she was no stranger to the dark evilness in this world with her first series, this was a new adventure for her and I feel she did an outstanding job.  She made it very clear to me in the beginning she wanted this story to be a realistic message of how far the system pushes teenagers who find themselves in foster care.  While what you are about to read isn't the usual outcome for those kids, what Gwen and Welch endures is common more often than should be allowed.  It was important to Mary that the readers see how far society pushes people into the blackness of survival only to punish them for what they had to do to stay alive.  I am very proud of her because I think she took a huge challenge and won with this book.

Gwens life suddenly changed at the death of her parents.  From being the beloved daughter and center of her parents world, she now finds herself with Claude and Helen, in a rundown trailer.  Her value in life was reduced to a monthly paycheck from the state.  With no one to care about her now, no goals for the future other than survive; Gwen has to reclaim a new identity, one that will help her find the fight to save herself.  She needed to discover the monster that was within her soul that she never wanted to nurture.

Welch is her new foster brother; he wants to connect with Gwen.  He knows the abuse that goes on in the trailer, he has suffered at the hands of Helen and Claude for too long, and seen to many other girls come and go.  Maybe with Gwen they can plan their escape as soon as they both turn 18. The time to run had come, but as with everything freedom doesnt come for free.  Life on the outside of that trailer wasn't any kinder to them and a new level of angst had begun to smother them.  When it came time to pay for their sins, they find they are also paying for the sins of every person who had laid a hand on them in the past or had forgotten that they were only kids who needed help.

I am not sure how you can read this book and not have your heart shattered by what is done to these two kids, who only wanted a chance to chase their dreams, finish school and know what high school love was like.  The author kept it real; she didn't pull any punches with the tragedy that Welch and Gwen call their life now.  Each was willing to become the monster the other needed in order to make it out of this alive.  I was impressed with how she weaved love into one of the darkest situations a teenager could fine, not the fly by night kind of love, but the self-sacrificing love that people rarely find or can give.

I strongly suggest you grab your copy of this book now, get some tissues and be prepared to find within yourself the power to change situations like this.

What a dismal beginning!  I thought, "Why am I reading this?"  Felt that way through chapter three, then it all began to come together and WOW what a read!  With the current headlines about politicians and their trespasses, this book illustrates just exactly what pundits are talking about.  Set in a small Southern town, our author has truthfully pictured the place of political power, gossip, neighbors knowing neighbors' business, and a non-professional sheriff with little or no training about how to handle the "real" problems.  While the characters are stereotypes, they play their roles perfectly.  The innocent young girl is the epitome of the all-American girl replete with a part-time job, a secret boyfriend, great grades, athletics, and even the doting daddy.  The sheriff is not a native but wins the approval of the town because of his fair treatment of others, his honesty, and his integrity.  The mayor has managed to marry money, spend his wife's money, gain power over the citizenry to the point of corruption, and seemingly has no conscience: he has managed to pull the wool over the eyes of the people who keep on voting him into power.  Add to this mix a deranged vagrant on a killing spree down I-95 and you have the unlikely makings of a story that will curl your toes, incite you to anger, provoke your conscience, and have you begging the author for just a modicum of honesty.  Then comes the powerful and totally unexpected climax that will leave you weeping with relief, cheering for the good guys, and totally aware of the place of happenstance. . .or is it Karma?  You have to read it.  You simply MUST read it.

If you remember your history, much of what we call Germany today, along with most of the Balkans, Poland, Hungary, Austria and even part of northern Italy were once part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire and they were famous for - among other things - their food, particularly pastries. Long ago and far away I had the privilege of living in Germany for several years. During most of that time my apartment was in the home of a wonderful German woman who became like a second mother to me. One custom that Lydia and her family observed daily was a coffee hour about 3 or 3:30 in the afternoon. Everyone who was available in the household and often a guest or two would gather in Lydia's living room for coffee and pastries. The simpler ones Lydia often baked herself and I was lucky enough to learn her recipes, recipes that I still use today. The more complicated things, though, were usually brought in from the Konditorei. Most days there would be just one or two offerings, but holidays and birthdays always brought a wide array of stunningly beautiful, marvelously tasty creations, some of which have haunted my dreams for forty years or so. The recipes for most of them are in Austrian Desserts and Pastries: 108 Classic Recipes, as well as recipes for many of the sweets we sampled touring Germany and Austria, and some specialties I'm unfamiliar with like Pumpkin Strudel and Rhubarb Strudel. The book is beautifully printed on quality paper and it features loads of color photographs of the final product. I did, however, find some problems. First, this book was translated from German and it is clear that while the translator is competent to translate, he is not a cook and definitely not a pastry chef, so some things have been translated literally but not well. Bear with me while I do a bit better of a job with some of those. You will often find something called "torte glaze" called for as an ingredient. In practical terms, the most generally available product is Dr. Oetker Clear Glaze, 2 Packets each .35oz. While some supermarkets do carry Dr. Oetker products, their Clear Glaze is not one that I have run across here in the US. You may have to order this online. The link that I included goes to just one of the several sellers here at Amazon that offer the product. You should not consider this an endorsement of any one particular seller. You may also need Dr. Oetker Vanillin Sugar (10 Pack) or Great Lakes Unflavored Gelatin Sheets (Dr. Oetker's gelatine sheets, which are made in Germany, are offered here on Amazon, but I cannot acquire a link for those). Most of the recipes also specify "flour(fine)" without stating whether the most acceptable flour available in the US is pastry flour, cake flour or 00 flour. Some attempt to translate the recipes from the original Metric measurements to US standard has been made, but the results are patchy at best and many of the recipes are inconsistent in the measuring system used. A "heaped cup" could easily range from an extra tablespoon to nearly an extra cup, depending on your particular idea of "heaped." For best results you will want to follow the metric measurements and will need a scale to weigh dry ingredients. There are a huge variety available in both manual and digital models across the whole spectrum of price ranges. Look for a model that "tares" - allows you to zero out the weight of the container so no math is required - and has a display with numbers large enough to see underneath your container, ideally one that measures as small as 1 gram and as much as 7+ pound (about 3 kilos.) Your standard Pyrex glass measuring cups have metric liquid measure on one side. Don't be surprised to find one recipe calling for a teaspoon of something and that immediately following it asking for 4 grams of the same ingredient. Finally - and hardly least - the recipes often either fail to give a pan size, stating only that a recipe makes "one torte of 12 slices" or call for a pan that most American home bakers will not be familiar with. The two most prominent of those are a Gugelhupf (Kugelhopf) pan and a rehrucken loaf pan. While these can be hard to locate, several versions of each are available here at Amazon. SCI Scandicrafts Kugelhopf Mold 9-inch 10-Cup is nearly identical to the mold in my kitchen and the Rehrucken Ribbed Loaf Pan - 11" Long is very similar and of the correct size for the recipes in the book. Both are eligible for Super Saver shipping. I've written to the publisher for clarification of pan sizes for the various cakes & tortes and will update this once I've received a reply. Additionally, one or two of the recipes call for a pastry frame, an item common to a commercial bakery but not part of the usual equipment one would find in even the most well equipped households. The least expensive available here is Paderno World Cuisine Adjustable Rectangular Frame Extender (from 11 Inch x 7 1/2 Inch to 21 1/4 Inch x 13 3/8 Inch), but at $57.26 you might very well want to leave this on the shelf and improvise. Austrian Desserts and Pastries: 108 Classic Recipes is definitely not a book for the novice baker by any stretch of the imagination, nor is it a book for those who are not comfortable switching between measuring systems. That said, if you have a bit of patience and a little knowledge of baking wizardry, the results for many of these pastries will be spectacular.

So, you might have noticed that I had reviewed a very similar sounding book not so long ago.  In fact, it was a very very similar version of this book, as in, the non-serialized version of this very book.

But, my friends out at iRead Blog Tours asked if I would be willing to give my thoughts on the serialized version of the book as well.  And, of course, me being the ever-willing pawn to folks trying to shill their books, I agreed.

As mentioned above, Kidnap is the serialized version of Guy Erma and the Son of Empire, which should be obvious from the full title.

There does appear to be some rather minor changes between the two versions, but overall, this seems to be purely the first act of the book which, I believe, is intended to now be split into three parts.

But enough of that, how about I get into reviewing this section of the book:

Everybody knows Guy Erma.  Well, almost everybody.  In fact, there seems to be only one person who doesnt have a direct knowledge of the titular character of this novel, the Son of Empire himself, Prince Teodor.  However, these two seem to have an ongoing relationship which continually works parallel to each other, until the Prince is kidnapped, of course.

Guy is led on a wild adventure attempting to seek out the truth of the Princes disappearance, as well as learning a lot of the dark inner workings of the government which may or may not have played a part in this kidnapping.

Im not much on political thrillers, but this book does have a fair portion of intriguing world building and edge of your seat adventure that its hard to mark it down for such a trivial genre issue.  That being said, the political pieces seem to get a little confusing from time to time, while also being altogether rather obvious.

My issues with genre aside, Melia builds a very interesting world, filled with enough unique items that one cant help but want to read further just to figure out more about the intricacies of this world, like, what is this Dome that they keep talking about, how do blades help you jump higher, and how exactly is Guy Erma so well known when he appears to come from such humble beginnings.

The end of this first book in the series seems to leave us on quite the cliffhanger.  We see Guy questioning how he got where he is, as well as attempting to determine what is really going onand what he has actually found himself in the middle of.

In other words, if you read the first book, youll definitely need to read the next.  And speaking as one who has read the whole thing, I can state that you won't be disappointed.  This is a fast-paced adventure that will leave you wanting for more.

As I have read each book in the Eagle Elite series, I have come to expect and anticipate an emotional roller coaster each time I enter the world of these Chicago mafia families. I also find friends - characters I have come to know and love, who have grown and changed through a multitude of difficulties they have faced together - because they are family. No one has ever been left to face hard times alone - family doesn't work that way.

I'll never forget when I first met Sergio in Elect (book 2 in the series). He was introduced by Nixon to Trace as "a ghost." She joked about his name - I joked about his name. By the time I finished reading Ember (the book just prior to Elude) I felt like I was just beginning to peel away the layers to discover just who Sergio is. Each book had given another glimpse into his character, but a full picture still wasn't formed.

Now, in Elude, Sergio takes center stage - all the layers are exposed and I found a very strong, loyal, tender man. A man with great depth of character. While he's definitely stubborn and portrays himself as a self-absorbed jerk, his new wife Andi manages to delve beneath the tough exterior and reveal not only the passion that lies within his heart, but the compassion and fierce devotion he has to those he loves.

Elude exceeded my expectations. I was thrilled with the anticipated emotional roller coaster and the fierce loyalty of the families I have grown to love. At the same time, I was pleasantly surprised by the sweetness of this love story. While it's all wrapped up in the madness of the Chicago mafia madness, at it's heart Elude is a sweet and tender love story that not only exposes the depth of love shared between Sergio and Andi, but also tears open your heart as you experience their love and their loss - as you experience their spirited beginning and beautiful end.

FYI ~ this is a New Adult book contains violence, mature language, and intimate scenes. Be sure to have tissues nearby when reading.

Before I start, you'll need to forgive me for any annoyance that may bleed into me review. I had typed a complete review a while back, fresh off of finishing the book, but lost it due to some idiocy on my own part. In addition, there are some spoilers within the review, though they are restricted to ideas that were especially interesting or presented problems, rather than what happens in the plot.
To begin, A Net of Dawn and Bones is a fun read. Overall, there are no glaring problems bogging it down, and quite a few things buoying it up. The action, inter-character development, and world-building are all interesting, and had me entranced from the start.
The novel is not without a few problems that, though minor, will prevent me from giving it a full five stars.
The first problem is one that I must admit, I feel a bit silly about raising. This is simply because I'm not entirely sure whether it's a problem of mine, or truly one with the book. Oftentimes, when characters are talking or thinking, they'll seem to cut out, as if what they were about to say next was obvious to them, but their enemies would have something to gain if they, too, knew. As a reader though, most of these instances left me confused, and again, I'm not entirely sure if the fault is mine or the author's.
Another issue with the book is that it opens the door to so thick a world of magic, religion, demons, and monsters, but explains so very little. We learn that there are four classifications of magic users, Wizards, Enchanters, Sorcerors, and some sort of elemental mage whose name escapes me. However, beyond the obvious powers of an elemental mage, and the power of wizards to see the future, we receive no real information on what, exactly, the differences between these are. Can wizards do anything else, or simply 'See?' What is the difference between Enchanters and Sorcerors? Again, it may be an issue of my not reading closely enough, but in this case, I highly doubt it.
Aside from these rather small problems, the work is an entrancing and interesting read. The story begins in Hell, with two of our main characters, Myrrh and Aiden. This chapter serves to define, more or less, what Aiden and Myrrh are, (though a few details are left out until later,) and introduces us to the idea of Hellraiders; essentially, humans who follow the example of Jesus, by descending into Hell upon death, finding those there that are undeserving, those dragged down by forces outside of their control, and hauling them out by their ankles. Soon enough, though, we find ourselves back on Earth... where someone is trying to open a portal to Hell, and Myrrh, Aiden, and Church, a detective who has dealt with the spooky side of things ever since Vampires, Werewolves, and other demonic entities revealed themselves and sought out protection under the law.
Many ideas presented aren't entirely new, but are interesting nonetheless. Vampires being corpses possessed by demons, and therefore not human in the slightest, in spite of their access to human memories, werewolves being (also) inflicted with a demonic curse, and True Names being a dangerous and efficient conduit for magical attacks are all old news, but have been missing the spotlight from most fantasy or modern fantasy stories for a while now.
The manner of narration is easy to read, and pleasant, save for those times that the book leaps ahead of you, thinking you can make the same logical leaps as the characters without access to the same information. Grammar and spelling are perfect, as far as a single read through can tell, and the characters are fleshed out so well, they feel like they could walk right off the page. The emotions and temptations felt by Aiden and Church especially feel organic, though it's not surprising that Myrrh feels larger than life... especially when looking at her history.
This book is definitely worth a read, and is worth the price of admission, so to speak.

I bought all of Susan Ward's books because I was totally addicted to Alan and Chrissie's story. I was hoping for a book that ties up their story. This is it! If you have read up to this point, you will remember the constant take and give in the whole series between Alan and Chrissie. They get together, they break up, they get together, they break up without anything really being resolved. Mostly on Alan's end.

This book will finally reveal all of the answers to the questions you probably have been asking like I was. And better yet, you read it from Alan's point of view. You finally get to understand the man better and my god, you will fall deeper in love with this man. You finally understand how wounded and scared he is.

The book hits a major point when Chrissie blows Alan away with a major shocking secret that was broken wide open in a way she did not expect it to be revealed. In a way it also brought healing to him which he did not realize that he needed. How easy it was breaking down his walls and make him complete again. But he did struggle a bit with the betrayal and the secrets that Chrissie hid. It made you understand that Chrissie had her own flaws and her own faults. But should this be the final straw for Alan? Whew. It is a major hurdle even when you understand why she did it.

When he asked her why she did not tell him earlier and she said that she was simply waiting for the right time, that she was saving them for him. God, that just broke my heart in a good and bad way. That made so much sense. It's true in a sad way. Just ugh, what a great little scene.

You also finally get to read about Kaley, the oldest child, and the struggles she was having with Alan. You do read about her in "Rewind." Be warned though, "Rewind" is a small jump in the future and deals with Kaley's own love story. Broken Crown is set in time behind "Rewind."

My only question that I was left with after reading this book is... All of them? HOW? Did Chrissie time it right or was she lucky? If you read the book, you'll get what I mean.

This culmination of the trilogy shows how someone who hits rock bottom, finds the strength to pull themselves together a build a better life.  This author takes Liam down a dark path, one he's known before.  With EVERYTHING taken from him, you feel the resolve it takes for him to do the right thing.

Liam's path back to the light isn't easy. He fights temptations daily.  He struggles through painful memories.  Yet, with the promise to do right by Tria and their baby, he battles his demons every step of the way.  The biggest being his revelation of what happened to him as a teenager.  It was pretty clear what had happened, but now we get every horrific detail and how actions by others, led him down the destructive path.

What I liked most about this book was how Liam made personal sacrifices to create the right life for his love(s).  He had opportunities to take his fighting career further, but his sole goal is to be there for his growing family.

The biggest surprise for me in this book was that Liam's parents weren't evil like I pictured them to be.  With little revelations, we see how they tried to make up for their mistakes.  And we see how deep their love is for Liam.  I was shocked by their own personal heartbreak, and actually felt bad for them.  Liam doesn't make things easy for them, AT ALL.  But they never give up on him.  And they never walk away.

On top of that  surprise, I was not happy with Yolanda.  I never really understood her story, and we get some of it.  But I didn't get how she gave up on Liam in every sense of the word.  I can't relate to how hard it would be to help an addict, but given some light shed on her, I couldn't comprehend why she couldn't help him anymore.  And her actions nearly cause his end, which can't be forgiven.  Later!

With Liam's personal struggle and growth, Tria benefits from his new life focus.  She becomes his biggest supporter, encouraging to stay with the therapy he desperately needed, and she helps to bridge the gap between him and his family.  The love the build together, supporting one another with each step, was very sweet.

Of the three books, this was definitely the most emotional one, as Liam's vulnerabilities are completely exposed.  His emotions were raw, and while he could be an jerk to those around him, most gave him a pass, knowing how hard he was trying.  With every page, I felt like Liam's personal cheerleader, wanting him to do right and find happiness.  This book ties up loose ends and leaves Liam in a place, that was long overdue.  A happy place.

Yolanda has a style and way with words that will completely engross you. Jude had a rough life. Yolanda is one of the best authors I've read, she captures emotions and her characters are so well built and thought out.

The description made it sound awesome with the "thin but strong paper can withstand Colored pencils, crayons and even your favorite markers. This one sided coloring book will allow you to tear the pages out for hanging, or you can keep them inside your book!"

Needless to say, with a kindle version, you don't have the luxury of coloring on a strong piece of paper and then tearing out for hanging. If you downloaded it to a paperwhite kindle, it's useless. If you downloaded it to a tablet, via the kindle app you may have a little more options. For me, my tablet includes Adobe Draw, so if I wanted to color on my tablet it might be useful. But I didn't want to color on my tablet. I wanted to get away from my electronic devices as a time to chill. Thus my excitement at getting a coloring book.

I really don't want to put the illustrator down for their work, but this was definitely not what i was expecting. Some of the drawings don't look as though there was very much follow thru put into them, and then others look as though they didn't go through a final editing piece.

I admit, I am tough on this coloring book because as  graphic designer I have to be tough, especially if I'm going to be making a purchase such as this. I'm just very thankful that as a kindle book order it was free. I would have been truly disappointed as a owner of the book. Author Lissa Pelzer leaves a note at the end of her sturdy debut novel that is about all the information we have about her. Lissa lives in Germany with her husband and son. And thats about it. This story is an attempt to write a modern day noir-ish piece of pulp in the style of the American classics. The city in the story is fictional but heavily inspired by Dayton, Ohio. There is something seductive about an author who speaks to her readers like that  and that is one of the primary reasons this book works so well. She is frank, no nonsense, serious about her skills, and writes like a pro.

Though NO MORE BIRTHDAYS is a stand-alone novel, the tagline suggests we are reading a created character who will be in an on-going series  the Carol Ann Baker Crime Book 1. When authors take the stance that reader s will want more about the heroine created, they must be rather sure the character works well. In the case of Carol Ann Baker Lissa has created a winner.

We don't even meet Carol Ann Brown (by that name) until later in her story  at first we meet Lilly Lessard  a young prostitute on a chase to find her pimp who has escaped owning her money. But as the synopsis states, Runaway teenager Lilly Lessard has some secrets. For a start, thats not her real name and she wants to keep her real age on the down-low too. Bumping into ex-hitman Bobby at a small town film festival is no coincidence either. Shes tracked him here. He owes her money and shes desperate enough to come looking for it. And shes not the only one whos followed him here. Detective Davis is after him too. Shes been after him in Miami for years, but never quite managed to get him. Maybe this weekend shell get lucky. But the closer Lilly gets to Bobby and his money, the closer Davis gets to them both. One by one, their secrets are coming out. And Lillys about to find out, the worst secrets are the ones you keep from yourself.

Lissas book has all the flavor of those 1950s crime films that remain so popular on the late night circuit on television. She knows how to weave a story, pop in interesting new characters as the plot unfolds, but always allow the show stopper heroine shine. This should develop into a very successful series of novels with a heroine like Carol Ann Brown at the helm. Its ballsy. Grady Harp, November 15

Nate Todd knows that the Crooked Tree Ranch has to get into the 21st century but with the way things are going, the ranch may not survive another season. When his brothers convince him to hire a marketing expert, Nate finds Jay Sullivan annoyingly citified and doesnt care for him. But Jay and his little family grow on him and his brothers as Jay figures out how to bring Crooked Tree Ranch into the new millennium. But when sparks fly between these two, can a city boy and country boy find a way to mesh their lives together in order to get their own happy ever after?

Author RJ Scott is a masterful storyteller who delivers a heartfelt and emotional story of two very different people who find their way to one another. Amid bumps and more in their road to romance, Ms. Scott delivers a story that will leave you breathless. The writing is tight, story flows smoothly and I got to admit the characters from the very beginning just stole my heart. I loved how city boy Jay got country boy Nate to take a chance on him even as the slow romantic development between the two got on my nerves at one time or another. All those sparks between them made me hope there would be no fires breaking out on my kindle. With all of this authors books, family is central and we got two families who are in flux in one way or another. I loved the dynamics of both Jays and Nates family and we got to spend time with both separately as well as together.

Its the characters that just make this authors books come alive. From the Todd brothers to Jays troubled family to the mysterious Marcus and his son who are also owners of the ranch with the Todd family to Sam the chef who wants his very own cowboy of his own. The variety of characters kept my attention and stole what was left of my heart-after the Todd brothers of course. This is an author who knows how to let her characters shine and show their vulnerabilities as well as their open heart to the readers. With their trademark writing style, Ms. Scott delivers a story that is full of heart and emotion as well as some serious sexual tension that I swear almost blew up my kindle. Overall, CROOKED TREE RANCH is one of those feel good stories that you cant help but fall in love with. Now I am eager to see where this author goes in the future books and hope we won't have to wait too long for them.

If you enjoy family themed stories with stubborn main characters, simmering sexual tension that will steam the pages of your e-reader then you need to get CROOKED TREE RANCH because RJ Scott just knocks this one out of the ballpark.

I was asked to review "4 Years Trapped in My Mind Palace by the author, Juhan Twiss, and this I've done willingly and honestly.  These are my feelings regarding this magnificently written story.

I felt the author wove this beautiful narrative in a heart-felt and humorous manner.  The characters are developed carefully, the settings are both sad and happy, and the conclusion gripping.

There are two main characters.  The first is Aaron, a 12 year old boy stricken by Cryptococcal Meningitis.  His parents were told that he was "brain dead" and would spend the rest of his life in a paralyzed and vegetative state.  He was placed in a convalescent home and spent the next two years able to see, hear, and think (contrary to the doctor's opinion).  During those years, in order to alleviate a life of boredom, he imagined a Palace in which he could explore and create imaginary adventures.

The second main character is Solomon, an elderly man in a progressing state of dementia.  He enters the convalescent home two years after Aaron.  Solomon has a saxophone named "Betty" which had been a large part of his life as a Jazz Musician.  Solomon becomes Aaron's roommate.  He has the ability to read Aaron's thoughts and ideas, and begins verbally communicating with him.

The two becom friends.  Solomon has episodes of dementia, and, surprisingly, Aaron becomes a character in various phases of Solomon's life.  Some of these phases include: the old man's childhood in Bronx, NY; A jazz musician, and leader of a band, meeting Dolores (who becomes Solomon's wife), and as a soldier during World War II.  Through these esperiences, Aaron learns much about Solomon's life, and shares the information with the old man, who has forgotten many parts of his life story.  Aaron also learns much about the world as it was before he was born.

Some of the experiences which Solomon had become adventures in Aaron's Mind Palace.

Solomon has a granddaughter, Sarah, who visits him almost every day, and soon becomes friends with Aaron, sharing her world and her schoolwork with him. And, like her grandfather, she talks to him.

Other characters in Aaron's life are Nurse Penny, who is amazed at the relationship developing between the boy and the man; Aaron's parents; Sarah's family; and some of the people whom Solomon knew during his lifetime. All become an integral part of Aaron's life.

Aaron is no longer bored and lonely, and manages to progress to a point of his doctor's and parents' disbelief.

I titled this superb story "The Gifts" because I felt that the author intended to show how both Aaron and Solomon gave each other the gifts of life.  Aaron's gift to Solomon was helping him remember his remarkable past, and Solomon's gift to Aaron was the gift of a renewed life.

I highly recommend "4 Years Trapped in my Mind Palace."  It is a book that I could not put down, and I completed it in one day. It enabled me to look back at places I've known, and to meet characters who reminded me of others in my own life.

Thank you Johan Twiss for this well written and inspiring journey!

Its been three months since Katys laid eyes on Mr. Tall, Dark, and Sexy with the very enticing accent. He walked into her club, strode directly to Katy, and practically seduced her right there in the middle of the dance floor. That one night she allowed herself to enjoy sexual pleasure, a much deserved night off away from the crushing responsibility of owning a club. Katy cant forget the one man who exudes power and a commanding presence, the one who owned her for one night.

Since the death of her father, Katy runs the club shes inherited from her dad, Amber Room, barely scraping by to keep it open. Problem is, the club is mafia-owned and shes come up short on the protection money. The three thugs sent to collect come with a warning threat, and Katys scrambling to find every bit of cash from her belongings. Ivan shows up, sexy as ever, and offers her a deal she cant refuse. Just her luck he happens to be her sex-on-a-stick one night stand, and to her horror, a Russian mafia hitman whose position in the organization is powerful. His deal: be his sex slave for a year. Oh yeah, shes owned by the hitman for a year in lieu of payoff money to the mob. But how bad can it be when shes screaming from orgasms, and not from pain of death? And, he offers his hard, muscled body for personal protection. Dayum !!

Owned By The Hitman is written in alternating POVs, though most of the narrative is told in Katys words. Ms. Abbott does an excellent job of presenting the following months as a series of vignettes they spend together as highlighted on New Years Eve, Valentines Day, and St. Patricks Day. At first, I was jarred out of the story, thinking I may have missed some pages, because initially I didn't sense how much time lapsed from the point she accepted the deal and New Years Eve. But thinking about it, it actually works very nicely, since Ivan sets up these surprise dates you get a sense of who he really is. Ivan is not what he seems. Hes tough and dangerous, but with Katy he is attentive and caring, very much the gentleman. Each date we see the growing attraction between Ivan and Katy changing into something deeper as they learn more about each other. When we get Ivans POV its when he is on a hit, and surprisingly he describes his disgust for the bad guys. Those chapters I found intriguing because Ivans words reveal that he has rules and morals which guide him. Wow, that kind of made him a hero in my eyes. He doesnt deny the bad stuff hes done, but he can never share the dark with Katy. For him, Katy is light to his dark, the warmth of home he yearns for, and I think for both, a little less lonesome.

I really enjoyed this story, it was well thought out, the pacing was perfect, and the engaging narrative grabbed me from the beginning until the end. Katy and Ivan are well developed and believable. A protective alpha male and strong female lead is always a winning combination, and don't forget the sizzling sex, yes, its hot. Enough to satisfy my inner bad girl. And she likes it plenty steamy. Theres twist in the plot line that I did not see coming; and my favorite is the absolutely romantic and sigh-worthy ending. All in all, a very entertaining read and one that I recommend. Great job, Ms. Abbott.

Ed has sworn off one night stands because they always make him feel like crap the next morning. Hes moving on to the next phase of his life. Ed is starting a new job and lives with his best friend in the city. He breaks his rule when Alecs wants to take him home. Their chemistry is too good not to give in. They end up spending the entire night together but Alec gives him the cold shoulder in the morning. It hurts Ed even though he knew it was coming. He tries to put it behind him and focus on his new job hes starting come Monday morning. Which just happens to be working under Alec on his big project.

This book was super sexy. Like smoking hot sexy. More and more lately Ive been skimming sex scenes in my books. This book infused so much emotion, want and need into every encounter between the two I loved every minute of it. There was a sense of urgency and finality because each time was supposed to be the last. They just kept coming back to each other. Their close proximity at work helped them get to know each other better and tease them endlessly. Alecs struggles with having feelings mixed in with his desire for a man for the first time in his life. So hes a little angry and inexperienced with how to handle the situation between them. That conflict of wanting something he shouldnt or cant have. I enjoyed how his character felt strong and confident but vulnerable at times also. He was so firmly in the closet he didn't realize how lonely he was until he met Ed. Ed was adorable. Hes out and proud but wouldnt ever expose Alec. Ed is very understanding of Alecs position but hes also not willing to be someones secret. So he tries his best to resist the attraction that burns so strongly between them. They of course fail miserably but they tried so tension was so damn good. And when they give in its amazing! Then they pull away again. This can be frustrating but for me this worked so well. The anticipation had me turning the pages. I loved the couple and their journey together.

Obviously I really enjoyed this one. Theres very little angst. Great characters that grow as the story progresses. Alec learns so much about what he really wants out of life and to get it he has to stop hiding who he is. Alec and Ed have amazing chemistry together. I love when you can feel yearning and how the guys cant get each other off their minds. The love story is realistic and sweet but balanced with all that delicious tension it makes this a really good story. I highly recommend this one.

Dogs that turn to humans.  Okaaaaaayyy.  A little nutty.  But I read the first book in the series and why not?  If humans can turn into wolves than why not dogs and why not dogs into humans?

But a former military dog who has lost his beloved handler in Afghanistan?  Sheer genius!!!  For one thing, oh, the angst!  But not so much angst, cuz, dog, you know?  They have it, but not like humans.  And Roman is only a few years out from being a dog who was the kind of dog that was ultra-loyal and smart and always with their handler and seemed to know more than most dogs.  He's missing his handler more than anything, he's depressed as he can be... Just trying to get along as a human, stumbling into the sanctuary for the "quickened" or dog-weres, where he finally finds a pack.  And a job.

He's now a Deputy and when the DEA sends agents to work with the small local departments in areas that back up into the wilderness where some drug operations are being set up, he is told to try and keep Matt out of town where he might see and suspect things about the quickened and busy checking out the wilderness.

So many cool elements to this story!  Love Roman's background story.  Love the whole law enforcement aspect--and military.  Love the whole trying to learn how to be human.  There is a bit of a TON of tropes in here, but it all works.  It is all more sweet and touching with some drug-grower danger and a bit of light humor.  Nothing heavy-handed or too angsty or dark.  Just a pleasure to read!
Wright is clearly a pretty good writer, but these stories had far too much "sameness" and became too predictable.  Hopefully his full length works won't have this problem.

Motivational books are not generally my thing. I mean, they should be because I'm severely lacking in that department most of the time, but my reading time has been very limited over the last year. This book was recommended to me by someone who knew I could use a big whap upside the head with the concept of "balance."

I wasn't sure what to expect, but I thought, "Hey, it's not that long. I can breeze through this, no problem."  The narrative style was refreshing, giving some example to the five main principles of the book. The rear portion of the book reiterated the points made during the character's story, which would be helpful to someone who didn't connect with the story itself.

My only issue--and I'm not sure how I would solve this--is that I didn't fully understand the explanations of some of the principles or how to apply them to my situations. This may just be my intellectual shortcoming, or I may need to read the book again with a fresh brain.

I read this book over the span of two or three short reading sessions, but it could be an easy afternoon read for someone with more than a few minutes to spare.

House of Shadows is a hard book to pin down to just a single genre. There is history, suspense, murder, romance and so much more.  I have only started reading historical fiction the last few years so I am no expert, but this is a really good multilayer story involving three strong women from three different time periods.
  Of the three women I think that I liked Holly the best but Lavinia is a close second.  Elizabeth is a good character but she seemed very selfish and shallow to me.  Holly and Lavinia were characters that I could root for and I was very intrigued by their stories and very curious as to where the story would take them. All three women are embroiled in controversy involving a secret society, a bejeweled mirror, a giant pearl with rumored magical powers, and love that seems destined to fail.
  There were times in all the periods that some inconsistencies popped up but never really over anything major.  Mostly it was small things that didn't really make sense or seemed out of place but I am not too nit-picky about small things so I was fine with it.  I think if you are looking for a good historical fiction book to curl up with this winter in front of the fire, House of Shadows would be an excellent choice.

review_text: Essential oils are still relatively new to me, but I never knew you could do so much with them. This guide takes you through everything that essential oils can create. It even talks about how you can start your own essential oils business and begin making money. The guide is comprehensive and starts off with an exploration of the history of essential oils. It then delves into individual types of essential oils and how they can be utilized to benefit you. There are so many different essential oils with so many different uses that I almost couldn't believe it! Toward the end of the book, you'll even find detailed and easy to follow recipes for a wide range of essential oil products. If you like working with essential oils, then you'll probably enjoy reading Simple Natural Cures: Cheap & Effective Remedies for Everyday Common Ailments. It works under the same basic idea of using natural elements to create cures for your body. We all know that essential oils can be used for curative or decorative functions. Sometimes, you want a natural treatment that works to cure a recurring malady. For instance, if you have a bad cough or indigestion, would you rather take a chemical-laden pill or something natural that you can make or find at a grocery store? In most cases, you'd rather use the natural treatment. Simple Natural Cures provides a wide array of potential cures for a variety of problems that you may face. I refer to it almost as much as I refer to my essential oils guide on my Kindle. Both offer some of the best information available on their subjects. Essential oils certainly walk hand in hand with natural cures and treatments, and I have certainly enjoyed my experience with both concepts. I have also enjoyed my experience with both books. The essential oils guide also provides information about the safe usage of essential oils, including which oils are approved by the FDA, which are toxic, and which can be harmful to infants. The easy to read charts also ensure that you'll never use too much in a recipe. This book clearly thought of everything and it's a great reference for anyone working with essential oils in any capacity.

If I were to rank my favorite ugly cry books, this is now my #1. I cannot think of any other book that compares to it. I am a very emotional reader and I love when I become attached to the characters. This story about Lena's and Nate's love not only had me hooked from the blurb, but more so from the very first page. If I didn't have to put down this book while reading it, I wouldn't have.

This book is written in both Lena's and Nate's POV. I think it was reading Nate's POV that crushed my emotions the most. The author did an excellent job writing from his perspective and all the emotions he felt were so raw. I've never been in his shoes, but I can imagine feeling everything that he did. To me, he wasn't written as a character that you swooned over or made into a book boyfriend. As a husband who loved his wife and always put her first in his life, he was perfect. He is the type of man who shows what kind of knight in shining armor you want by your side. He was romantic and passionate, strong and honest. And just perfect.

And Lena's POV. She was very much a wife who thought of her husband before she thought of herself. From their trip to Europe to all the doctor visits, she didn't ever put herself first. As I read her real life dilemmas and decisions made, I could truly feel with each one the love that she had for Nate. A love to last both their lifetimes. My heart ached and broke, yet I was also happy for her that she had a husband like Nate.

There were many many chapters where I cried throughout the whole chapter. To be honest, I think I spent most of the book in tears. Towards the end of the book, I learned that I not only needed a case of tissues, but I should have taken off my mascara too. This book will stay with me, and I know it's a book that I will reread because everything that this couple went through was everything I would ever want to read in a love story. It was not a typical Michelle Leighton read, but she nailed this story. It goes without saying that I found this to be a 5 star read.

If you're looking for a short PNR read with lots of intrigue and a hot hero, this one is for you! The Dragons Temptation holds all the tropes I love about PNR like the insta-love connection and the brooding alpha but this turned out to hold so much more. What I expected to be a run of the mill story of a magical connection with loads of hotness became a story of two star-crossed lovers of Romeo and Juliet proportions.

The ladies who make up Lily Cahill know how to mix the sweetness of their romance with interesting characters and tense plots and this one was no different. I hardly settled into the connection between Felicity and Damien before the hits started coming. Fast-paced and laced with old family secrets it held my attention and kept me turning pages. I loved the lore of this little novel and especially because it was unclear who was on the right side of the fence.

The Viking Spirit by Daniel McCoy was my second venture into Norse "religion" and Mythology. The book is probably as good a place to begin as any when digging into what actually remains of pre Christian Norse beliefs. The book is divided into two sections, the first one hundred twenty pages or so deal with Norse religion, followed by one hundred fourth eight pages of Norse myths.

Dealing first with the myths, McCoy precedes each myth with an introduction to the myth, possible sources, possible Christian and or Middle Ages influence, and an educated guess at how much of the myth might actually be from original sources. This is a nice touch for those who might want to dig further for themselves for a more thorough interpretation.

Norse religion, is addressed in the first portion of the book. McCoy is right up front about Norse religion in that it was never "systematized or codified during the Viking Age", nor was it recorded in a written language. The same can be said for the Viking myths, as the myths were not standardized, and the myths changed over time, and by different influences even within the Viking "nations".

Using an analogy, think of a paleontologist, who finds a smattering of bone fragments, some larger and more complete, some hardly there, others missing entirely, mixed with other fragments of a different creature. He/she then attempts to piece together the original find, based upon incomplete skeletal remains, and then attempts to bootstrap together how that creature lived. That is my impression of the challenge facing the scholars who's goal is to compile Norse religion and mythology in their original forms. McCoy even rationalizes that the reader can invent their own means of interpretation and understanding of the Norse, as the beliefs of the Norse were constantly evolving.

In closing, this was my second venture into Norse mythology. My first voyage was The Norse Myths by Kevin Crossley-Holland, about three years ago. I prefer the Crossley-Holland's work, if for no other reason, that it was my first experience with Norse myths. Rather than preceding his myths with an introduction to each, his note section, following the myths, he deals with each myth. KC-V also provides much more information in his note section for the interpretation of Norse mythology. If one is interested in understanding the Viking world through their  mythology and religion, I'd submit that McCoy's book is the place to begin, then read Crossley-Holland's work. After that, if still wanting more, each author provides sources for further research.
summary: The Remnants of The Viking Spirit

The title, The Dragons of Alsace Farm by Laurie Lewis, was deceiving and I admit that I for one was expecting a story with a paranormal bent.  But what I got was something totally different and so far from what I normally read I was skeptical on whether or not I would enjoy it.  I didn't just enjoy it I will be putting this book on my list of favorites to re-read.
Noah Carter has had a tough life, a rough childhood and the loss of his personal hero have done a number on his self-confidence leading him to a solitary lifestyle repairing washing machines in a laundromat for room and board as well as working a full time construction job.  All of this in order to maintain an isolated existence.  Noahs happy with the life hes built for himself and doesnt plan on changing anything about it, that is until he receives a message from his Uncle to come home.  Noah agrees reluctantly and is reunited with his Uncle John and Aunt Sarah, his uncle is extremely ill and asks for Noahs help with a few things, one of which is to help his elderly neighbor, Agnes, around her farm.
Agnes Devereaux Keller is an 80 year old WWII survivor, widow who is suffering from dementia but refuses to give up on her home.  Noah and Agnes become good friends in no time, Agnes is given someone to interact with and share her knowledge and Noah is given someone to take care of that loves him unconditionally plus he knows how to deal with Agnes when her memory gets shaky, its truly a match made in heaven.
Tayte is Agness granddaughter who has come to Alsace Farm to take care of her grandma.  Taytes own upbringing was bad, with parents who couldn't seem to care less about her.  Her one shining memory was of her eighth summer and the grandmother on the farm, how she felt loved and protected on that farm.  Unfortunately the grandma from her memory isn't the same person anymore and Tayte has a hard time adjusting to the changes ending up handling Agness dementia all wrong many times.
There are so many things that happen in this book, so many side stories that are told, so many secrets revealed (typical of a small town), so many secondary characters that are important to this story, I could go on and on.  I highly recommend this book; it was such a pleasure getting lost in Ms. Lewis writing.  This book was a true pleasure to read and if I could give 10 stars I would.

review_text:
I liked this and I gave it a good rating (for me) and if I had read this a year, a year and a half ago or more maybe it was a 5/5 stars.

The Writing:
I liked the writing, it felt kind of classical YA. It had one POV and maybe i would have liked to read from Viggos POV. It was easy and fast to read, quite entertaining, I wouldnt say life changing but it was a good dystopic book.

The Story:
I really liked the idea of the story. Its set in a world that after wars was being reconstructed but women and men had different ideas of the new society to come. That ended up having two countries with monarchies. We have Matrus, a country where women are ruling and are in charge, men have less rights and have almost no position in society. On the other hand is Patrus, a society ruled by men and they have all the positions and careers, women are almost pets, not allowed to go out withouth a husband, speak or do anything by themselves.
I think the world was unique, the idea was different and surprised me. We got to know a lot of these countries though I believe a bit more of Patrus.
Our main character is convicted to almost death and so she accepts a mission for her country in Patrus, where she is supposed to be married to Lee, a Matrus man but living in Patrus as an spy.
The story in its development was good. It had action and surprised me many times because things I didn't expect happened most of the time. It keept you in a stress kind of mood because everything was on the line, all the action and the spies, not only the monarchy was an enemy the people from Patrus were an enemy too.
Other thing we had was the romance. This was a classical YA romance and I enjoyed it soo much. Nothing more than a kiss but all the tension and romance that built through different moments was great. I could see from the first moment who would be the love interest and couple but that is fine too because I had to see them develop their emotions.
The ending was a complete surprise. I didn't expect any of the things that happened to happen and that left me wanting more. I want to know what happened to some characters, I want to know what will happen, what is the truth, and all the answers I don't haveyet.

I think we could say this was a kind of action/spy story (which I don't usually read and was great), the most original thing for me was the world. The romance felt like a classic YA, which was not bad for me but it didn't have any surprise there. There was action many times that made the story more fast paced and it had you in a kind of stress level all times.

The Characters:
I have to say this (and Im happy to say this): is easy in YA and most of all these kind of fantasy that some character (usually the main one) is frustrating or at least a couple of times while reading it you want to *facepalm*. I think that didn't happen to me.
Violet: She was young but she did what she had. I liked her, I liked that she was not blind by any kind of loyalty, she used facts to lay her loyalty. There were just a few times I think I said: don't do that but she did anyway and I had to read it and well, Im just a humble reader. I think she will develop a lot more as a character in next books and Im really loking forward to that. I feel like she did grow but she could have grown a lot more. She learned about love and how people can lie to achieve what they want. The ending leaves you wondering whats coming for her and I think she can become an amazing character.
Lee: You ended up being a surprise. He was a mastermind, very intelligent and only he knew what he really wanted.
Viggo: I liked him a lot. We know him but I hope we get to know even more. He wasn't the romantic type, he was more wild but serious. And I really want him to open and I think when that happens if the author does things well he can be an amazing character.

Overall this was an interesting setting, with a classical YA romance, for me fast paced and easy to read.

Shel: I'm not sure there could be a more perfect time to release a book about politics. Politically Incorrect is especially interesting as it makes many apt references to current politicians and the circus that appears to go on behind the scenes. As you can see from the synopsis below, this novel gives us a peek behind the curtain of what happens in a political race with the added benefit of a 'forbidden' romance to add to the tension of whether Liam Baxter will become the next Senator of Texas or not.

Shel: The two main characters, Elizabeth and Liam, are an interesting contrast. She's aggressive, a little more closed off,  and more inclined to do the dirty stuff for the job and not flinch. Liam on the other hand, is much milder--saving his aggression for the things he deems really important, seems completely open, and is a unicorn in politics--he believes in being honest and above board. As different as they seem, the heated banter and disagreements quickly turn into heated looks and touches and before you know it, there's hiding their lust in order to avoid any possible scandal.

Shel: If you're looking to escape the toxic political environment in real life, this steamy romance might be just the thing to distract you.

I am giving Widowers Aura -- A St. Fleur Novel-- Book One, by AJ Renee, a four star rating for a fantastic story.
  AJ Renee really knows how to write a small town and the people in it.  She made St. Fleur live by populating it with real down to earth people.
  Noah, Sophia and their friends and relations come together in an ultimately feel good story about love, life, and getting to know about both.  Sophias character is amazingly well written.  Ms. Renee manages to write Sophia as sweet, smart and sexy.  Noah is all hot, sexy alpha male.  His tortured past is well developed and the story moves well from Noah to Sophia.  Ms. Renee never skips a beat or misses any of the nuances that happen between the two love birds.
The tension between Noah and his daughter is very sweet and filled with the many misunderstandings that often happen between fathers and daughters.  Especially when tragedy haunts their past.  The loss of Noah's wife, Lexies mother is powerful and felt throughout the story as Noah comes to grips with his life going on in spite of all the heartache in his past.  In trying to put his daughter always first, he has managed to put himself and his needs last, denying himself and his needs.  That is until he meets Sophia.
Sophia might just be the person who can piece this relationship between Noahs daughter and himself back together.  If she gets a chance to try.  Her past seems to be catching up to her too, and not in a good way.
Widowers Aura is a sweet love story that has a few twists and turns before the end is reached.  It is a terrific shorter read.  Perfect beach book.  I really like Ms. Renees handling of the past trauma in Noah and his daughters lives and how that trauma potentially affects the rest of their relationships and their lives.  When you lose someone it never goes away, it just becomes more bearable over time.
I really enjoyed Ms. Renees treatment of loss and renewal of love.  Four Stars all the way for Widowers Aura.

This is one of the deepest books by Byron Katie.

She uses personal examples from her experiences, opening up like never before.

If you're new to The Work (Katies techniquefour questions and a turnaround), I wouldnt necessarily recommend starting off with A MIND AT HOME WITH ITSELF.

As far as non-dual teachings go, Katie is about as radical as they come, with the exception, perhaps, of Tony Parsons.

What I love about Katie is that she provides more than some theoretical discussion on non-duality. She offers a clear practice in the form of what she refers to as The Work.

This is the experiential side of everything she talks about, and it is for everyone, even kids, if they are open to it.

The Work can be used (or seen) as a self-help technique, or it can be used as a big step in the direction of spiritual freedom.
While Katie does give an example or two of applying The Work, the practical aspect is not the focus of this book as it is with most of the other books shes written. A MIND AT HOME WITH ITSELF describes in intimate detail the experience that is the freedom revealed through The Work.

It is similar in many ways, to a previous book she has written, A THOUSAND NAMES FOR JOY. Both books offer Katies interpretation of ancient texts translated by her husband, Stephen Mitchell.

Whereas A THOUSAND WORDS FOR JOY examines excerpts from the Tao Te Ching, A MIND AT HOME WITH ITSELF probes one of the crown jewels of Buddhism, The Diamond Sutra.

This book knocks it out of the park, it really does.

I'm a HUGE fan of Jade Summer's coloring books, and I was very lucky and delighted to get a free PDF copy of this book for my review. :)  So, disclaimer goes there, the print copy might be different!

This book is full of such BEAUTIFULLY detailed pictures.  They have SO much personality and a lot of movement and... Ooh it's so nice. :)

There are several canine pictures and while canines aren't normally my favorite things to color, these ones have such...  such...  personality.  There's a howling wolf, a panting coyote, a sly looking fox...  I love it!  A lot of the images are very dynamic, using angles rather than profiles or straight on.

A little more critically, there are a couple of pictures that are...  I wouldn't say were reused exactly, but. for example, there's a close up of a howling wolf's head-- just the head-- and another one that is a howling wolf, with the front half of the body, and some neat flames or grass or something and a background and stuff.  The head-only shot would be an easy 'short' project, while the other is a full page image an would take a lot more time.  The same deal happens with a gorgeous Llama--though there's not a full body shot there, just a complex background.

I've spotted  this happening several (4?) times in this book and that's a bit of a bummer, honestly, though the pictures that are "duplicated" in this way tend to be some of the more beautiful ones, so I would be glad for the chance to color some of them twice.... But still!

But past that, the art is, as ever, amazingly detailed, with fun patterns tracing over fur and feathers alike.

As for the contents:  By my count, there are 12 canines (ranging from French bulldoggies to wolves and all points in between) 15 birds, 9 fish, and about 5ish horses.  And a collection of others, including monkeys, llama, a squirrel and a bee, as well as a few others. :)

Love it! :)

4.5 stars. Misha Lare and Ryen Trevarrow have been loyal pen pals for the last 6-7 years, having grown up together through letters that shared everything with each other. Best friends who have never met in person nor know what the other looks like, their relationship is preserved in a safe cocoon. Until they actually do meet. The setup of the story is brilliant because Misha knows exactly who Ryen is, but Ryen has no idea that Masen, the new guy at school, is her Misha and she hasn't heard from Misha in a long time. And Misha is appalled that the version of Ryen at school is nothing like the girl in her letters because the one in front of him is not the sort of person he'd ever be friends with, but he adores the girls who writes to him. And both Ryen and Misha have their own personal issues, aside from all of the high school drama. There's multiple layers to this story with hidden twists and surprises. I loved the dialogue and tension in the way that only Penelope Douglas can write it. Misha was a jerk at times, no doubt, mainly to push Ryen out of her facade and to just be her real self again. How the foundation of long time pen pals lead to this modern day antagonism with secrets and revelations really fueled the story because I was always waiting for the next thing to happen due to the build up, and when it did, it didn't disappoint in terms of execution, emotions or excitement.

Watching him struggle with a love he so desperately craves but does not think he will ever deserve broke my heart over and again.

Secrets. Betrayal. Confessions. That sweet reunion.

I don't mean to be a harsh critic when I review books, but I recognize the value of an honest review. Too often that translates to my reviews being a bit brutal. Before I started 'Rhapsodic,' I just gave up on a book I had started and was simply too irritated by the 2-dimensional, cookie-cutter manic pixie roommate and clichd heroine and main man to finish it.

So I was in a foul mood when I started this book. Imagine my surprise  (and not a small bit of wonder) when Laura Thalassa grabbed me immediately and drug me into her world of blood and murder and very scary men. Now that's a hook! Add a well-timed reference to Shakespeare, a fantastic description of the desperate of a murder, then a best friend whose crass mouth and fresh characterization blew away so many other poor, trite characters in other PNR and I'm yours. Hook, line... well, you get it.

The heat between Des and Cassie was - OMG! I think my hair is singed. Please don't tell my husband, but I think I'm a little in love with the Bargainer. And I don't like blondes.

The pacing of the story was enough to royally screw up my sleep cycle. So, yes, Ms. Thalassa, my husband may not be so pleased with your book. And you've published more! I'm SO excited!

For a 1st person POV novel, the author somehow managed to create a voice that was fresh, unique, and never monotone, which is quite a feat if you've ever tried writing in 1st POV. The humor was fantastic. It never felt forced and it brought another level of charm to Cassie. Come to think of it, I may be a little in love with her too. Uh-oh. *wink*

The heat level was mature for certain and, oh so, hot, but not overwhelming. Thalassa manages to make gentle fun of the typical romance read at times, calling out things like codependent behaviors (because that's exactly what they are) and being perfectly irreverent about things other authors might wax purple about. So refreshing.

The whole concept was really quite unique too, which might be the very best part. I honestly put books down if I see the word 'vampire' in the blurb lately. Paranormal romance has become so predictable and unfortunately, boring. And it's about the most imaginary of imaginaries, for Pete's sake! How can it get so trite? But, never fear, Ms. Thalassa has woven a dark and magical tale about fae and sirens and werewolves, and not once did I think, 'oh yawn.' Absolutely magical.

If I had to find a flaw, it would be that the author doesn't put commas before addressing names and titles. Mostly just grammar police nerdery. The other thing is why are there only a hundred some reviews of this book? People are missing out. There should be thousands. Seriously.

It appears the book is the first in a series. Thank God and, What!?!? Number 2 isn't out yet? Nooooo! Don't despair though, things wrap up nicely, if not completely. And while everything isn't perfect for Cassie and Des, it's good enough to sleep at night until the next installment. And you better believe I'm reading that! In fact, if Laura Thalassa needs an early reviewer or a beta, I'm so in. You rock!
Now that I've read the first three, I can't wait for more. Romantic and just a little heat. Great series.

Adriana Locke has a gift of writing not only intense, emotional roller coaster style books, but also lighter, tender stories with emotion that still reaches deep inside and grab you by the heart. Swing is the latter...

We met the powerful, talented, handsome Landry family in Sway. In Sway, we are introduced to Lincoln, the athlete of the family. A major league ball player with a major league body and ego. Linc is all alpha and cocky, but often in a laugh out loud way. I couldn't help but love this ego loafed hottie with a very sensitive, sweet soul.

When Lincoln discovers Danielle, the sexual tension explodes off the page almost immediately. But Danielle has a painful past that causes her to desperately fight off Linc's advances, but have no fear - he wins her over. And it's there that the story takes off in a way that kept me glued to the page. She so wants to ignore her feelings and do what's 'right', but how can she ignore her perfect man right in front of her?

This may be a lighter story for Adrianna, but lighter doesn't mean without depth and emotion, and a whole lot of laughs and sexy yumminess. Love this story and loved the peek at the rest of the Landry family. I cannot wait to read the next story in this wonderful series.

Kyle and Nicole are two very different spices and face all the hate and prejudices x10. They each face physical & mental torture. They are fighting every supernatural evil being possible, even family, but because of their love for each other they overcome and learn forgiveness for themselves and others. This is truly a love story. We witness the sacrifices Nicole made for those she loved knowing they would hate her. Kyle was willing to give his life to have her love for just a moment if that was all he could have. I love how love and goodness won. The author brilliantly showed how the hardships of life shape the people we become and love and happiness comes when and where we never expect. I must go back and read books 1- 3.

Holy Crap! This book grabbed me with a seriously intense prologue and never let go. I could not put it down!
Corbin and Vi had the sweetest of sweet relationship. Her innocence, his patience. They were young and in love. First love is beautiful and theirs was no exception.
They taught each other. He helped her grow and mature. I loved watching her come into her own. She showed him he could love and was able to be loved. Both broken in their own way but fixed once together.
Then we are hit with a draw dropping ending!! Beginning to end this book was so good!! Now I not so patiently wait to see what happens after the lie!! I need the Truth Revealed NOW!!

In some ways the story seems familiar at the beginning (reminds me of The Giver). But you are dropped into the scene and have to figure out what this world is like, so maybe I was looking for something familiar.), As it unfolds this book moves in a different direction than other dystopian fiction I've read. The characters are very likeable and relatable. Around 20% in it seemed there was repeated backstory, but after that the story really took off. (And it was clean of typing and grammar errors.) I look forward to book #2 and hope it continues to build. Warning: the story is not clearly resolved at the end. You get a certain amount of closure, but new questions arise in the final chapter. Those who want the story wrapped up in one book will not like this. But you aren't left completely hanging if you choose to not continue the series.
