The introductory line of the synopsis for Honey Bee states that love can either be as sweet as honey or sting like a bee, and after having finished this first ever Heather Shere read of mine, I must say that those were wise words indeed. It doesn't even necessarily have to pertain to just the aspect of love but it speaks of life in general and the events that occur in our life. We aren't always guaranteed happy ending or even positive results, but if you don't take those risks or open yourself up to something new or different or to plain, old change, then you may never get to experience that sweet part of life. This love story truly was sweet and with the bonus of addition of a frisky dog named Triton who knows how he's the king of his human mama's world, it was a heartwarming and light romance.

Yep, I admit it. Triton was my favorite thing about the book. But then if you know how much of a dog lover I am, that tidbit shouldn't be too much of a surprise. That isn't to say that that was the only thing that I liked about the book. This didn't have the usual bitter-about-love theme nor was this about unrequited love or broken hearts. Bo's reason for not wanting to be around animals is a heartbreaking one, although I did want to smack him each time he was a jerk towards Triton, who clearly just craved his attention AND affection. Heather Shere put her own spin on things, making this a more refreshing read than most, although it felt as if something that was hinted at early on fizzled without explanation. Honey Bee gets four stars, and I do hope Lawrence Miller gets his own story as well.
This story had many twists and a real surprise ending but brought everything together at the end in a very satisfactory way.

review_text:
Firstly, if you haven't read book one in this series then you really need to in order to understand this second instalment from this series and my review may contain spoilers if not too.

I feel like Ive been stood at my window twitching at my curtains waiting for this book to find out where the author takes this story after the bombshell ending to the first book. As such I was happy to see that we pick the story up right where we left of and are pulled back into the situation between Katya, Liam and Wulfric. Katya is understandably hurt and angry, Liam appears sorry and Wulfric is..well Wulfric.
What we see more of in this book is Katya concentrating more on herself and the initial reason she got into this mess, of stepping out of her shell, happens along the way. Katya is reeling from what the two men did to her and as she works out the situation and what is best for her she turns the table on Liam and Wulfric and plays her own game back on them.
What we get is a fab read with plenty of angst as well as laughs at the banter between the three of them but also plenty of development in these characters along the way. We learn more of Liam and Wulfric and why they are the way they are. At times, I wanted to shake Katya but I get why she chose the path she did and I think it works out better for them all in the long run. At times, I felt they should all just walk away and at others I wanted them to just agree to a three-way relationship as they all vied for the right choices. In the end, it takes some wise words from someone outside of the triangle to help Katya decide what she wants and needs and I was happy with the outcome of this instalment of the series.
After meeting new characters in this book Im curious as to where they will fit in to the overall series and as such I am already eagerly awaiting the next book.

Brilliant plot, engaging characters, and a ripping pace.  I have been reading mysteries for 50 years, and have a few favorite writers.  It is such a pleasure to find a new one.

When Sheikh Salilk receives information that his grandson Sheikh Yuusuf is involved with a young woman believed to be a fortune hunter he sends his older more sensible grandson Tal to rescue Yussuf.  Tal decides the best way to do this is to Impress the young woman with his charm and wealth convincing her he would be a much better catch and therefore rescue Yuusuf from a bad situation, then breaking it off with the fortune hunter. But Sheikh Salilk was given misleading information and was mistaken.  Meanwhile Talique is proceeding with his plan to win the heart of Laura while Yuusuf is actually involved with Laura's best friend Jenna.  When the mistaken identity is  discovered Tal comes to the realization that in the process he has lost his heart to the lovely Laura.  Now he must pursue her in earnest to earn her trust and love.  Will he be successful?  I received an advance reader copy of this book and this is my honest review.

This is a great story by Barbara McMahon, one you will enjoy reading.
summary: Assumption can lead to mistaken identity
